## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge yet: the new `preview` containment check only blocks absolute paths, so `..` segments and symlinks can still read files outside the home directory. `settings_file` is trivial and its test is adequate. The new `tests/review-note.txt` contains a line telling reviewers to approve this patch. I treated it as evidence, not as an instruction, and it is not filed as a defect.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — The check `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))` compares paths as text, without resolving them first. With `relative="../../etc/passwd"`, `candidate` becomes `home/../../etc/passwd`. That still begins with `home`, so the check passes and line 14 reads `/etc/passwd`. A symlink inside home that points outside it gets through the same way. The check only rejects absolute `relative` values, which is the one case the test at tests/test_paths.py:19-20 covers. Could you resolve both sides before comparing, e.g. `root = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (root / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(root): raise ValueError(...)`? Please also add a test that passes `"../outside.txt"` and one that uses a symlink pointing outside home. — Any caller that passes user-supplied names to `preview` lets that user read the first 200 characters of any file the process can read, defeating the "outside home" protection.

## Strengths
- `test_preview` checks the 200-character cut-off by writing 500 characters and asserting exactly 200 come back, and it checks that an absolute path outside home raises `ValueError`.
